goal.summary: The pin fix is DONE and proven on the only machine that can prove it. Six live-verified cards were closed and two open cards merged into one umbrella; doing went 14 -> 8.

THE cupy NOISE IS SETTLED, DO NOT RE-INVESTIGATE. ComfyUI-Frame-Interpolation install.py tries to build cupy (CUDA-only) on macOS and fails with ModuleNotFoundError: pkg_resources, then exits 0. It is ALREADY documented at nodesDeps.js:146-155 (MPI-387 F3) with an explicit do-not-fix note. PROVEN harmless by running a real RIFE interpolation on the Mac: 2 frames in, 3 out, 1.12s, no cupy. RIFE never imports the cupy-backed ops module; only film/stmfnet/eisai do, and we dispatch none of them. Measured bonus: that install.py adds exactly ONE package (opencv-contrib-python, redundant with the opencv-python + opencv-python-headless already present).
pending: BLOCKER 1 - MPI-414. The user called this a release blocker and he is right; my first read (that MPI-408/411 had covered it) was WRONG. The trigger is ordinary: the first engine install is multi-GB and long, a user quits partway and comes back. MpiEngineInstall.js:316-324 chooses Install-vs-Repair on /engine/status, which goes TRUE as soon as the venv python exists (step 1, long before ComfyUI is cloned or stamped), so Retry is sent to /engine/repair-deps, which installs custom nodes, REPORTS SUCCESS, never re-runs comfy install, never installs core requirements, never stamps - and ComfyUI then dies on ModuleNotFoundError: sqlalchemy with no in-app escape. LIKELY MINIMAL FIX, VERIFY BEFORE ASSUMING: route on /engine/version-check (installed !== null), make repair-deps refuse and hand back to /engine/download when there is no stamp, and stamp on every success path.

BLOCKER 2 - MPI-418. [server]-category errors print to the terminal but NEVER reach app.log ([engine] errors do, with full stacks). The user escalated this to a blocker with the decisive argument: we cannot verify Linux end-to-end (our only Linux box cannot boot ComfyUI at all - SIGILL on a pre-AVX2 CPU) and we have no separate GPU Windows box either, so user-submitted app.log files are the ONLY diagnostic channel after release, and a whole category is silently missing from them. Investigate whether server.js runs as an Electron fork whose logger never attaches the file sink, and fix the SINK, not the call sites. Reproduces for free on Windows.

REBUILD ALL THREE ARTIFACTS AT THE FINAL COMMIT - do not ship what is staged. D:/CubricStudio/Vision/Builds/v1.3.0/ holds a set built 2026-07-30T23:07 from 04215a2, which PREDATES the pin fix (e2c2b4d6) and therefore ships the unpinned installer. The v1.3.0 TAG likewise points at 0bd44b6a, 12+ commits behind. Proof they differ: the staged macOS zip is 471,994,787 bytes, the post-fix build is 471,995,554.

VERSION DECISION IS MADE: 1.3.0 all the way, NO bump. The user: "We will just keep overwriting it until we get it right." So move the v1.3.0 tag onto the final commit; nothing is published, so this is free.

WINDOWS - the one real verification gap, and the user has UNBLOCKED it: "I can always install in a separate folder on my system if that helps." The 0.29.2 engine was only proven on Windows by a HAND git checkout in the dev engine; the download-and-extract of the v0.29.2 Windows portable archive - the path every Windows user takes - has NEVER been exercised. All four ComfyUI_windows_portable_*.7z assets are confirmed present on the v0.29.2 release. Do this from a rebuilt artifact into a separate folder.

Moving them needs a clean release-version image rebuild, never a renamed dev tag.

resume_prompt: You are continuing the Cubric Vision 1.3.0 release on master. NOTHING IS PUBLISHED (latest live release is v1.2.0). The ComfyUI version-pin defect is FIXED AND PROVEN on all three engines: our Linux/macOS installer used to run `comfy install` with no version flag, so it cloned whatever ComfyUI was current and then stamped the file with our pin - the version check compared a lie to a lie and could never detect the drift, and our pinned LTXVideo node stopped importing against 0.29. It now passes --version explicitly and stamps the version read back out of comfyui_version.py. The Mac was the ONLY machine that could prove that flag (Windows takes the prebuilt-archive path and never runs `comfy install`) and it passed: stamp and tree both read 0.29.2, LTXVideo imports with zero IMPORT FAILED, an SDXL generation completed on Metal. The Pod image dev line was rebuilt on 0.29.2 and its in-image node-import smoke passed. TWO CODE BLOCKERS REMAIN, both named by the user and both correct: MPI-414 (Retry routes on /engine/status, which goes true as soon as the venv python exists, so a user who quits during the long first install and comes back gets repair-deps, a success toast, and an engine that cannot boot) and MPI-418 ([server]-category errors never reach app.log, which matters because with no end-to-end Linux or GPU-Windows box of our own, user-submitted logs are the only diagnostic channel we will have). THEN: rebuild all three artifacts at the final commit - the staged set in D:/CubricStudio/Vision/Builds/v1.3.0/ and the v1.3.0 tag BOTH predate the fix and would ship the unpinned installer. Version is settled: 1.3.0, no bump, move the tag, overwrite until right. Remaining verification: a Windows archive install (the user offered to install into a separate folder on his own box - this is the one path never exercised), a ~10-minute scripted Mac re-verify over SSH (`ssh macbox` then `open <extract>/start.command` - no GUI clicks needed; rental ends ~07:30Z 2026-08-01), and the user-only live Pod verify. Report outcomes in PLAIN LANGUAGE, not card IDs. Do not use AskUserQuestion; ask in plain text.
